If you only need a data plan, you can call through apps (VoIP), such as WhatsApp, FaceTime, and Facebook Messenger.

  • Security: Enjoy safer browsing with built-in security features like virtual location, ad blocker, and web protection against malicious sites and trackers.

Frequently asked questions about Europe eSIMs

Figuring out what the best Europe eSIM is comes down to your budget, the length of your trip, and which countries you plan to visit. The Saily eSIM app is a great choice for a Europe trip — you’ll get to enjoy competitive prices, automatic plan activation, an option for auto top-ups, and three built-in security features that add a layer of digital privacy to your browsing experience. Saily’s ad blocker feature even helps you use up to 28.6% less of your data, allowing you to stretch your plan further!

Absolutely — having speedy mobile data handy at all times will make your trip around Europe much smoother. With an eSIM plan for Europe, you won’t have to worry about searching for a SIM card in person or encountering sky-high roaming fees by enabling your international roaming. All you have to do is download an eSIM app, pick the best plan for your trip, install your eSIM, and start browsing. If you’re going with Saily, we recommend installing your eSIM before you leave for your Europe trip. As long as you’ve turned on your eSIM via your settings and enabled roaming for this specific plan, you’ll have internet access the moment you arrive in the first country included in the Saily Europe data package.

Yes, as long as your device is eSIM compatible. Most smartphones and tablets manufactured after 2019 support eSIM technology. However, if you’ve purchased your device in a country with eSIM restrictions (e.g., mainland China), then your device might not support eSIMs. Not sure about yours? See our list of eSIM-compatible devices. If you’ve purchased a Saily eSIM plan for Europe, you’ll get coverage in 35 countries.

While the benefits of an eSIM outweigh the drawbacks, some disadvantages include:

  • Your device needs to be eSIM compatible. While most smartphones manufactured after 2019 support eSIMs (including the iPhone [11 or later], iPad [released in 2019 or later], Samsung Galaxy [S20 or later], Huawei P40, and Xiaomi [12T or later]), not all do. Browse our list of eSIM-supported devices if you’re unsure about yours.

  • Transferring an eSIM between devices requires more steps compared to a SIM card. While it’s possible to transfer an eSIM between devices (even iOS to Android and vice versa), it’s less straightforward than popping a SIM card into another device.

  • If your plan is data only, you won’t get a local phone number. Saily currently offers data-only eSIM plans, which means you won’t get a local phone number to make calls or send texts. That said, you can use VoIP apps like WhatsApp, Signal, or Viber to stay in contact with friends and family.

Finding a SIM card with coverage across Europe can be tricky — travelers tend to buy multiple local SIM cards for each new country they visit. A much more convenient alternative is to get an eSIM (virtual SIM card) for Europe through an app like Saily, where you can find flexible travel eSIM plans starting at just US$3.99. With a Saily mobile data plan for Europe, you’ll get to enjoy high-speed coverage in 35 countries. After you’ve installed your eSIM, make sure you’ve turned it on in your settings and enabled roaming so that you’ll be instantly connected to the internet once you arrive in the first country covered by the Europe plan.

Is getting an eSIM for Europe worth it?
Absolutely — having speedy mobile data handy at all times will make your trip around Europe much smoother. With an eSIM plan for Europe, you won’t have to worry about searching for a SIM card in person or encountering sky-high roaming fees by enabling your international roaming. Will my eSIM work in Europe?
Yes, as long as your device is eSIM compatible. Most smartphones and tablets manufactured after 2019 support eSIM technology. However, if you’ve purchased your device in a country with eSIM restrictions (e.g., mainland China), then your device might not support eSIMs. Not sure about yours? See our list of

What are the disadvantages of using an eSIM?
While the benefits of an eSIM outweigh the drawbacks, some disadvantages include:
Your device needs to be eSIM compatible.
While most smartphones manufactured after 2019 support eSIMs (including the iPhone [11 or later], iPad [released in 2019 or later], Samsung Galaxy [S20 or later], Huawei P40, and Xiaomi [12T or later]), not all do. Browse our list of eSIM-supported devices if you’re unsure about yours.
Transferring an eSIM between devices requires more steps compared to a SIM card.
While it’s possible to transfer an eSIM between devices (even iOS to Android and vice versa), it’s less straightforward than popping a SIM card into another device.
If your plan is data only, you won’t get a local phone number.
Saily currently offers data-only eSIM plans, which means you won’t get a local phone number to make calls or send texts. That said, you can use VoIP apps like WhatsApp, Signal, or Viber to stay in contact with friends and family.
